newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator voices support for FCC candidates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator voices support for FCC candidates.

text.p: A key Republican senator voiced support Thursday for the three candidates that members of the Senate have sent to the White House for consideration as nominees to the Federal Communications Commission.

"Obviously, I'm pleased with the three nominations," Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, told a news conference. McCain chairs the commerce committee, which will vote on any White House nominations to the five-member agency.

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Mississippi Republican, last week sent to the White House the names of House Commerce Committee Chief Economist Harold Furtchgott-Roth, Justice Department lawyer Michael Powell, and FCC General Counsel William Kennard.
Furtchgott-Roth and Powell would fill two Republican seats and Kennard would fill a Democratic vacancy.
It is unclear when President Clinton will decide on the final FCC nominees. McCain said he would like to hold hearings on the choices in June and to act on them "as soon as possible."
